text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — seeing p95/p99 latency spikes from private VPC small-gpu pool (t4-small class) when continuous batching is enabled with low token_budget_ceiling. Noticed more kernel-fallbacks in the profiler.

Ashwin R.: Which model and typical seq lengths? Any KV cache churn metrics?

Maria G.: Llama2-7b-q4, mostly 1-32 prompt tokens, generation 128-512. KV cache eviction counter is high on these hosts, and the kernel-selection log shows repeated fallback from optimized attention -> generic slow kernel around step ~48.

Maria G.: Quick paste from the host profiler:```
kernel_selector: attention_opt_v2 -> fallback_generic_attn (count: 112)
kv_cache_evictions: 86
cpu->gpu memcpy spikes: 12 @ 3-6ms
batch_formation_wait: avg 4.2ms, tail 20ms
```

Sophia L.: Interesting. On small GPUs the kernel choice cost can beat batching gains for some slice shapes. Two immediate knobs to try: increase batch formation window slightly (eg from 4ms -> 8ms) to allow better pack density, and lower token_budget_ceiling per-request so tiny requests don't hog the slot. Also add a soft queue_length cap to favor filling slices with similar seq lengths.

Ashwin R.: Can you show the current VPC override config for that pool? I want to propose exact values.

Maria G.: Config snippet we currently run (private override):```json
{ "batching": { "formation_window_ms": 4, "token_budget_ceiling": 256, "queue_soft_cap": null, "slice_pack_strategy": "greedy" } }
```

Sophia L.: Proposed changes for experiment A:```json
{ "batching": { "formation_window_ms": 8, "token_budget_target": 64, "token_budget_ceiling": 128, "queue_soft_cap": 12, "slice_pack_strategy": "seq_bucket" }, "kernel_priority": ["attention_opt_v2","attention_opt_v1","generic_attn"], "kv_cache": {"eviction_policy": "lru_per_slot", "max_slots": 512} }
```

Kevin T.: Run it as a canary on one host first. Need perf diffs: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, gpu_util, kv_evictions. Also check model quality/regression with existing eval prompts (small risk if token_budget changes reorder micro-batches).

perf-bot: [alert] deploy-2026-02-12 created kernel change kernel-schedule-v3; hosts with t4-small show +8% p99 on averaged test-suite. See /ops/releases/2026-02-12 for details.

Ashwin R.: Good catch, @perf-bot. That kernel scheduling change likely bumped the fallback heuristics. For the canary I'll also flip kernel_priority to favor older opt_v1 for small seqs and keep v2 for long sequences. Suggest rule: if avg_seq_in_batch < 64 => opt_v1, else opt_v2.

Maria G.: Noted. I'll schedule the canary now: one host in eu-west-private-smallgpu with experiment A plus kernel_priority rule and kv eviction tuning. Will run for 2 hours then promote if tokens/sec stable and p99 improves.

Lisa Ops: Make sure to add a runtime override in the Private console path: vpc->pools->smallgpu->overrides.batch.knobs and pin the canary host id. Also add a short rollback playbook in case GPU OOMs or tail latency regresses.

Kevin T.: Add metric checks: decrease in kv_evictions by >=30% OR p99 better by >=10% for promotion. Otherwise revert. Also capture kernel selection histogram for rollup.

Maria G.: Will post results here. Quick smoke after flipping: p50 1.8ms -> 1.6ms, p95 12ms -> 9.4ms, p99 48ms -> 36ms (preliminary, 10m sample). KV evictions down 40%. Looks promising.

Ashwin R.: Nice! If stable, we should template the seq-length-based kernel_priority rule into the runtime so VPCs can opt-in. Could expose as "kernel_policy: dynamic_by_length" with params.

Sophia L.: Agree. Also file a follow-up to tune slice_pack_strategy heuristics — seq_bucket helped here because it reduced cross-length packing that forced slow kernels.

Maria G.: Filing perf thread and RFC for the dynamic kernel policy + default overrides for constrained pools. Tagging owners: @Sophia L., @Ashwin R., @Lisa Ops. :thumbsup:

Lisa Ops: Thanks—I'll prepare rollback and a quick runbook for customers who want to opt into the canary.

perf-bot: [note] canary run started 1891234567-1, collecting metrics -> will report after 2h.

Maria G.: Closing the loop later with full numbers, but initial canary looks good. Thanks team.
